items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: And I had a seat with me, Henry Ford, me, Henry Ford Ambrose, and his son, Barty Ford.

ctx.x: Was he a valve trombone player or a slide? A valve. Valve at that time. Yeah. So we went on down there playing on there.

Well I didn't have many children to play. Got the booty, Casey Jones. And one or two numbers. I could play. The rest I couldn't play. How did you come to get the job? How did they come to hire you? They hired me because he dis-actualy someone I would make the crime for him. So he can't get on me. And I did want to live. Let's see who was an ugly old man for who. Let's see, who's the ugly old man Ford?
Do you have a hood of him? Mm-hmm. Henry Ford, I know.

items.title: Emile Barnes Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: So, Buckland had a play. So, I went down there after crossing out. Went down there to him.

ctx.x: Oh, really? So, uh, Dundee Taylor, it used to be on the farm.

Uh-huh. So, I stopped in there, and they got to recess with them, and they, I called them down to get a drink. They come along and got a drink, and a bunch of women's in there and men. All the drinks for the house. So, when I bought the drinks for the house, well, I bought the drinks with me. Paid for the walk out, and, uh, I could get drink, drink, and have people's milk. All the way down, it was. So, Buckland had a play. So, I went down there after crossing out. Went down there to him. He, uh, told him I wanted…
What kind of flute was that?
